findings.reason: F3 identifies n with encoded input length, while the definition promises all Boolean functions on 2^n addresses and the query-instance/algorithm suppliers index oracle access by encoded instance length. A full truth table has length N=2^n and there are 2^(2^n) possible tables, so the stated family cannot be encoded by all length-n inputs. De Wolf §2.4.1 likewise takes an N-bit oracle table with N=2^n. The smallest missing prerequisite is an owner decision separating address width from encoded instance size, or an abstract oracle-instance convention; this cannot be reconciled on this page alone.

The proof infers that at least N/2 addresses remain unqueried from |S|≤N/2 and |{0,1}^n|=N, then selects the first N/2. The actual def-finite-cardinality supplier does not state the complement-counting rule, and the item supplies no local derivation. Add a finite counting argument for the complement size and selection; the theorem statement need not change.
